response:
I am running the mail test suite with a simulated non-ASCII hostname to observe the failures.
I have resolved the issue where email messages crashed with `UnicodeEncodeError` when using a non-ASCII domain/hostname with a non-Unicode email encoding:

1. Added [`punycode()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x43lgp9w/django/utils/encoding.py#L268-L270) in [django/utils/encoding.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x43lgp9w/django/utils/encoding.py) to convert non-ASCII domain names to Punycode (`domain.encode('idna').decode('ascii')`), and updated existing IDNA conversions in [django/core/validators.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x43lgp9w/django/core/validators.py), [django/utils/html.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x43lgp9w/django/utils/html.py), and [`sanitize_address()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x43lgp9w/django/core/mail/message.py#L105) to use it.
2. Updated [`CachedDnsName.get_fqdn()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x43lgp9w/django/core/mail/utils.py#L16-L19) in [django/core/mail/utils.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x43lgp9w/django/core/mail/utils.py) and [`EmailMessage.message()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x43lgp9w/django/core/mail/message.py#L255-L262) in [django/core/mail/message.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-x43lgp9w/django/core/mail/message.py) to convert non-ASCII domain names to Punycode.
